tb21_profile.skill: Express an exact whole-file text transformation as Vim normal-mode keystrokes and ex substitutions stored in registers, under a keystroke budget, escaping them correctly inside setreg() and running headlessly.
tb21_profile.domain: Vim / ex: registers and macros, Vim's own regex dialect, :%normal!, headless invocation (vim -Nu NONE -n -Es -S); large CSV text.
tb21_profile.task_form: Implement-from-spec under a hard resource budget (optimise-for-a-budget), with byte-for-byte output equality and a restricted allowed-command list.

verifier_notes: I found no grade I disagreed with on inspection here. notes: This is the clearest case in my five where a new corpus beats the old pool outright. The v1 pool (56k tasks) contains essentially no Vim editing tasks - 'tools.py search all vim' returns nine hits, all of them incidental mentions of vim as one of several editors, plus one 'build VIM from source'. Terminal-Lego-15k has a dense, mostly strong-graded cluster of tasks that drive Vim headlessly in ex mode and check output byte-for-byte (task_063xx family), which is exactly this TB2.1 task. Eight of my final ten are Terminal-Lego and that is the honest answer, not a quota artifact. CalibForge's contribution is the sed-program task, which captures the 'program using only the editor's own primitives' constraint. SWE-Smith and SWE-Rebench have nothing here; their entries are filler with overall 1-3 and should not be read as endorsements. TerminalWorld also has no Vim content beyond tw_17688 (building Vim).
